cluster_summary: A collection of 18 vulnerabilities where HTTP endpoints lack proper authentication or authorization checks. The root causes span missing authentication guards, missing permission annotations, missing object-level ownership verification, insufficient privilege validation, and other authorization bypass issues, allowing unauthenticated or unauthorized access to sensitive operations.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-selected resource identifiers, object IDs, tenant IDs, or administrative action targets into sensitive read, write, mutation, deletion, workflow, or administrative operations on the selected resource. Report code paths where the authorization decision is not bound to both the current principal and the exact resource or tenant being affected. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 8 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should check ownership or tenant scope before the effect and carry that checked identity into the data access or mutation.

mechanism.missing_guard: the authorization decision is not bound to both the current principal and the exact resource or tenant being affected
mechanism.name: missing object-owner or tenant-scope authorization
mechanism.sink_shape: sensitive read, write, mutation, deletion, workflow, or administrative operations on the selected resource
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-selected resource identifiers, object IDs, tenant IDs, or administrative action targets
mechanism.typical_fix: check ownership or tenant scope before the effect and carry that checked identity into the data access or mutation

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add the appropriate permission annotation to each method to enforce role-based or permission-based access control.
sub_patterns.name: Missing permission annotation on controller methods
sub_patterns.root_cause: Controller methods are accessible to any authenticated user because they lack fine-grained permission annotations (e.g., @RequiresPermissions, @SaCheckPermission), assuming authentication alone is sufficient.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add an ownership or membership check (e.g., verify user owns the object or belongs to the resource) before performing the operation, or remove the vulnerable endpoint.
sub_patterns.name: Missing object-level authorization (IDOR and ownership check)
sub_patterns.root_cause: Endpoints use user-supplied resource identifiers to fetch or act on objects without verifying that the authenticated user owns or has permission to access that specific object.
